title: Aurumix Gold Savings: Simulation Results
subtitle: What it takes for the business to be profitable, how much to raise, and what can be given back. Two thousand seven-year paths over two hundred thousand simulated customers.

intro: The business works, but not the way the plan describes it. It is a B2B platform whose retail book is the product partners sell. Retail alone does not cover its own fixed costs at any size the market can supply, and three configuration changes are worth about USD 1.18m off the raise.

stats.label: Raise needed, nine paths in ten, with the three changes
Odds of clearing the hole by year seven
Partners that cover the fixed base by themselves

findings.title: Partners are the business
findings.body: They are 31% of year-seven revenue and the top of every sensitivity ranking. Remove them and the seven years lose -USD 4.17m and the funding need rises to USD 5.74m. It is the one failure no raise can fix.

findings.title: Only one region pays for itself
findings.body: India returns USD 14.92 per customer a year at an acquisition cost of USD 13. It covers the whole company's fixed base with 23,475 customers, against the 48,240 the plan already builds there. The UAE and the Gulf lose money on every customer. Blending all three into one acquisition cost of USD 44 hid it.

findings.title: The plan sits exactly on the frontier
findings.body: At today's acquisition cost it needs 11 partners and plans for 11, landing at USD 0.17m of cumulative profit. A 17% overrun on acquisition costs three more partners.

findings.title: Real customers skip months
findings.body: The book pays in 78% of the months it could, so revenue per paying customer is USD 32 rather than the USD 38 an always-pays model gives. Retail alone would need 146,289 customers to carry the fixed base.

findings.title: Gold is not the risk
findings.body: A 30% crash is almost indistinguishable from base. Customers own the gold and Aurumix earns fees on flows, so the price exposure sits with the saver. The credit book is quiet too: the chance of ever needing a collateral top-up is 4.1%.
